_meta.what_this_is: Two systems whose TRUE pass rates differ by a real, useful margin: A passes 70% of cases, B passes 76% -- a genuine 6-point improvement. The question is how many eval cases you need before that difference is detectable rather than lost in noise. Each sample size's minimum detectable effect (MDE) -- the smallest difference an eval of that size could distinguish from zero, roughly the 95% CI half-width on the difference -- is computed and compared to the true 6-point effect.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The true rates are the ground truth (in reality you would not know them; that is the point -- you must reason about detectability before running). Every standard error and MDE is computed in power.py from the rates, the sample size, and z. small_n and large_n are the two sizes the self-test contrasts; z=1.96 is the 95% two-sided critical value.
_meta.format: rate_a, rate_b (true pass rates); sample_sizes (n per system to evaluate); small_n, large_n (the contrast); z (critical value).
